audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed final' (final stress) rests on Kruspe & Hajek 2009 JIPA, the specialist phonetic description; the quotation is verbatim at p. 246 of the PDF downloaded now (previously no copy held, and the record's cite/loc/grade fields were blank with the source only in 'sources'). Action: fill cite/loc (JIPA 39(2):241-248, p. 246), point to the PDF we hold, and assign an strength of the evidence. Optional refinement for the compilers: the source states stress is 'non-distinctive and predictable.. fixed on the final syllable' with no exceptions mentioned, which would support strict fixed: final syllable rather than 'fixed-dominant' (not in the strict set) if the non-strict flag was set only for want of an explicit no-exceptions statement; stress domain w.r.t. clitics is not stated in JIPA, so 'domain' stays not yet coded pending Kruspe 2010.

sources.citation: Kruspe & Hajek 2009, Mah Meri, JIPA 39(2), section 'Stress and syllable weight' (Cambridge Core, doi:10.1017/S0025100309003946)
sources.quote: Word-level stress is non-distinctive and predictable: it is fixed on the final syllable which in turn is always bimoraic (heavy).

sources.citation: Kruspe, Nicole & John Hajek. 2009. Mah Meri. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 39(2): 241-248. doi:10.1017/S0025100309003946 (open access on Cambridge Core).
sources.quote: Word-level stress is non-distinctive and predictable: it is fixed on the final syllable which in turn is always bimoraic (heavy), e.g. /luˈwat/ 'mangrove worm'. As a result, stressed final vowels in open syllables are lengthened – they are usually fully long, but can also appear optionally as semi-long.

sources.citation: Stevens, Mary, Nicole Kruspe & John Hajek. 2006. Register in Mah Meri: a preliminary phonetic analysis. Speech Prosody 2006, Dresden. doi:10.21437/speechprosody.2006-65 (ISCA archive, open).
sources.quote: No statement on word stress (paper is on the two-way voice-register contrast; notes register-2 vowels restricted to the final syllable). p.1: 'Mah Meri, also known as Besisi' (identity confirmation).

sources.citation: Moran, Steven & Daniel McCloy (eds.). 2019. PHOIBLE 2.0: inventories 'Mah Meri' UZ 2201 (contributor Steven Moran) and EA 2347 (contributor Dmitry Nikolaev), both sourced from Kruspe & Hajek 2009. Jena: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History.

sources.note: Database record read: inventory of 58 segments = 30 consonants + 28 vowels (oral, nasal and nine breathy 'Register 2' vowels such as ɑ̤ e̤ i̤ o̤ ṳ), segment-class filter 'tone' returns zero entries, i.e. PHOIBLE codes Mah Meri with no tonemes and treats the register contrast as vowel phonation; primary source named on the page: Kruspe and Hajek 2009.
